name: Increasing Devotion
oracle_text:
Create five 1/1 white Human creature tokens. If this spell was cast from a graveyard, create ten of those tokens instead.
Flashback {7}{W}{W} (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then exile it.)
blocked_sentences: If this spell was cast from a graveyard, create ten of those tokens instead.
Flashback {7}{W}{W} (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then exile it.)

needs.what: A card-level `flashback` field carrying an alternative mana cost (`{7}{W}{W}`) that legality offers only for a copy of the card in its owner's graveyard, replacing the printed `{3}{W}{W}` rather than adding to it, plus the once-only rider that the spell goes to exile instead of the graveyard when it resolves or is countered
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `retrace` is the only field that widens legality to scan the graveyard (`legality._cast_actions` loops `state.players[pid].graveyard` on `card.retrace`), but it is a bare boolean: `CardDef.retrace_cost` is hardcoded to `Cost(discard=1, discard_selector={'types': ['Land']})` and `game.py` charges it *in addition* to the printed cost, so it can name no alternative mana cost at all — Increasing Devotion would cost `{3}{W}{W}` plus a discarded land instead of `{7}{W}{W}`. Retrace is also deliberately reusable, returning the card to the graveyard, which is the opposite of flashback's exile. `kicker` is a real string cost but is additional, paid from the hand, and never changes which zone a card may be cast from. `suspend` names an alternative cost but plays the card from exile on a counter countdown, not from the graveyard on demand. The `replacements` whitelist covers only enters-the-battlefield shapes, so nothing can replace a spell's move to the graveyard, and an `exile` op in `spell_effects` cannot stand in because it would fire on the first cast from hand too, exiling the card before it could ever be flashed back. Same need filed under this slug for Deep Analysis (`data/authoring/gaps/deep_analysis.json`), which additionally needs a `pay_life` component in the alternative cost; Increasing Devotion needs only the mana half, so one field satisfying both is a full cost, not just a mana string.

needs.what: A condition readable inside `if`, of the shape `{"cast_from_graveyard": true}` (equivalently `{"flashed_back": true}`), that is true exactly when the resolving spell was cast from its owner's graveyard — so one card can do strictly more on the flashback cast than on the cast from hand, without duplicating the card
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `{"kicked": true}` is precisely this shape and precisely this plumbing — a per-cast flag chosen on the action, carried through `stack.push_spell(..., kicked=action.kicked)` onto `EffectContext.kicked`, and read in `conditions.evaluate` — but it is welded to the `kicker` cost, and the loader actively rejects a `kicked` condition on a card with no `kicker` (`loader.py:215`), so it cannot be borrowed to mean anything else. `zone_is` reads `ctx.state.objects[ctx.source_oid].zone` — the source's *current* zone, which for any resolving sorcery is the stack, identically whether it was cast from hand or from the graveyard, so it cannot tell the two casts apart. No selector, value expression or binding records a spell's cast-from zone either. Note this need is distinct from the cost need above and does not fall out of it: an engine could implement flashback casting completely and this card would still be unimplementable, because it would create five tokens on the flashback cast instead of ten.
